tagline: Three miles from a governor's spring to the Jamestown ships.
intro: A short one, about three miles. Centerville and Greensprings roads come down from near the old Green Spring plantation to the Jamestown Festival Parkway, a state highway only a third of a mile long, which meets the Colonial Parkway near Jamestown.

Green Spring belonged to Sir William Berkeley, one of the least popular governors colonial Virginia had, who tried flax, rice, silk and spirits there as something to sell besides tobacco. The plantation saw Bacon's Rebellion in 1676 and a battle of the Revolution in 1781.

moments.title: Green Spring Plantation
moments.text: Only remnants are left of Berkeley's house of 1645, but the spring still runs, so cold that a visitor in the 1680s thought it dangerous to drink in summer.

moments.title: Jamestown Settlement
moments.text: It opened as Jamestown Festival Park for the 350th anniversary in 1957, the year Queen Elizabeth II came, and keeps replicas of the Susan Constant, Godspeed and Discovery.
